requirement: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, except for the header option lines of {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap in `requirements.ci.span`. All the supplied tests carry `{test}` references to it. I did not request implementation source.

**Opening fence (at least three colons, immediately followed by `{req} <name>`)**
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent]` rejects `::{req}` (two colons), `:::{req}ready` (no space before the name) and `::: {req}` (a gap before `{req}`). It also rejects `    :::{req}` (four-space indent).
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers]` accepts openings of four and seven colons.
- The same function checks `requirements.ready` is counted once, so the opening is recognized.

**Closing fence (at least as many colons, nothing else but whitespace)**
- `validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers` covers equal and longer closers: `::::` with `::::`, `::::` with `:::::`, and `:::::::` with `::::::::`.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive]` shows a shorter `:::` does not close a `::::` block. Its body keeps the nested `:::{note}…:::`, and the block is closed.
- `closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent` shows `:::foo` does not close, and `::: ` with trailing whitespace does.
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence]` covers a missing closing fence.

**Indentation of up to three spaces**
- The same lib test accepts a three-space indented opener and closer.
- It rejects a four-space opener.
- It shows a four-space `    :::` does not close, so the block stays unclosed.

**Body is all Markdown between the fences, except anchor option lines**
- `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` includes a code block containing `:::`, an ATX heading, a `##` heading, a Setext heading and blank lines. It compares the exact recorded body.
- `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` includes a code block containing a `{req}` role.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text]` checks that `:impl:` and `:test:` lines immediately after the opening fence are excluded. It also checks that the same text later in the body, such as `Text :impl: inline.`, stays in the body. A nested example's options are also stripped.
- `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable]` asserts that evidence containing only the body, without option lines, gives no "text changed" error.

**No text after the closing fence**
- `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` puts "Outside the requirement." after the first block and checks the body without it.
- `validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers` does the same.
- `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` checks that `Outside.` falls after the block's end.

**Whitespace trimmed when comparing**
- `requirement_bodies_are_compared_without_surrounding_whitespace` uses a body with leading blank lines and indentation plus trailing spaces, against trimmed evidence.
- `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` also has a leading-indented body.

**Ambiguity I considered**
- `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` expects a `:::` line inside a code block not to close the requirement. The requirement text could be read either way on that point. The requirement says the body includes "examples" and "diagrams", which supports the test's reading. I do not count it as a gap.

text: :::{req} span

A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, except for the header option lines of {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
For each `:test:` anchor, the harness MUST include the selected file or node's
source text in the initial model request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and MUST record that selection
as an evidence input under {cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`,
so changing that source makes the evidence stale.
A `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
